We have seen multiple reports of Apple Vision Pro being used in medical settings. This week, Stryker announced that it has completed the first surgical procedure using a brand-new application on Vision Pro.

The surgery was a hip arthroscopy, using the SportSuite Vision application, which brings "key digital content into the surgeon's virtual space." This includes arthroscopic imaging, HipCheck, HipMap, and CT scan images.

The following is Stryker's description of the application:

SportSuite Vision brings key digital content into the surgeon's visual space, allowing them to view digital tools such as arthroscopic imaging, HipCheck, HipMap, and CT scan images simultaneously while still seeing physical objects in the operating room. During arthroscopic surgery, surgeons often need to rely on multiple displays placed at various locations in the operating room to access video images and surgical data. By integrating multiple data sources into the surgeon's field of view, this technology can reduce reliance on traditional displays and support a smoother, more ergonomic surgical workflow.

SportSuite Vision received FDA De Novo authorisation on July 17. Stryker stated that this application is the first FDA-authorised application for use with Vision Pro during surgery.

Also this week, Pfizer announced that they are using Apple Vision Pro to "create a memorable, immersive experience" to "showcase" their determination to "conquer cancer."
